purpose: Execution plan for adding a /goal feature to this Go Claude Code implementation after comparing current Codex and Claude Code behavior.

codex_goal: Official Codex docs describe /goal as a persisted goal for a task, available in CLI, IDE, and desktop surfaces.
Documented commands include /goal <text>, /goal, /goal edit, /goal pause, /goal resume, and /goal clear.
The objective is used as the task target and completion criteria; the documented max objective length is 4000 chars.
The goals feature flag is marked stable and enabled by default for persisted goals and automatic continuation.

Current-session Codex tool APIs expose get_goal, create_goal, and update_goal with statuses such as complete and blocked plus optional token budget. This is verified runtime behavior, not public implementation source.
claude_code_goal: Official Claude Code docs require v2.1.139+ for /goal; the latest changelog observed during research listed 2.1.209.
/goal is documented as a session-scoped wrapper around a prompt-based Stop hook.
After each turn, a small fast model evaluator checks the goal condition from transcript only, with no tools or file reads.
If the evaluator says no, Claude starts another turn with the evaluator reason as guidance. If yes, the goal clears and an achieved entry is recorded.
The goal does not change permissions. Unattended operation still needs auto mode or equivalent permission policy.
Active goals restore on --resume or --continue, while achieved or cleared goals do not restore; counters and token baseline reset.
local_repo: No built-in /goal command is currently registered in commands/builtins.go.
Slash commands are registered through commands.RegisterBuiltins and surfaced to TUI suggestions from the command registry.
SessionMeta in session/session.go is the natural persistence point for a goal sidecar.
loop/query.go already has a no-tool-use branch that runs Stop hooks and token-budget continuation, which is the natural continuation insertion point.
loop/stop_hooks.go already models Stop-hook blocking feedback as a user message and continuation.

comparison.project_choice: Persist goal state in SessionMeta, but evaluate it inside the existing loop Stop-hook window.

comparison.codex: Public docs expose controls and persistence, but not the evaluator internals.
comparison.project_choice: Use an explicit GoalEvaluator interface with transcript-only tests and fake evaluator coverage.

comparison.codex: set, view, edit, pause, resume, clear.
comparison.claude_code: set, status, clear/aliases; replacement starts immediately.
comparison.project_choice: Implement Codex-style controls because they fit persisted session state and reduce risk during long local work.

comparison.codex: Same sandbox and approval policy as the task.
comparison.claude_code: Does not change permissions; combine with auto mode when desired.
comparison.project_choice: Never let /goal change permission mode; document that explicitly and test no permission bypass path.

comparison.codex: Better for durable task orchestration, UI state, pause/resume, and budgeted work.
comparison.claude_code: Better for a lightweight continuation MVP because this repo already has Stop-hook style continuation.
comparison.project_choice: Hybrid: Claude-style evaluator loop plus Codex-style persisted controls.

waves.notes: Define the domain contract before implementation.
Independent tests for persistence, command, evaluator, prompt context, and tools.
Implement the surfaces proven by wave 3 tests.
Wire shared runtime paths. Keep concurrency low because repl_tui.go and registry_setup.go are shared files.
Add final loop behavior and TUI projection after runtime wiring exists.

dispatch_rules: Dispatch at most six subagents concurrently.
Do not dispatch tasks that write the same file in the same wave.
Treat tasks with dependencies as blocked until every dependency is accepted.
Each task is designed for 1-5 minutes of focused implementation or test work.
If a task finds that its owned file is dirty from another actor, report upward instead of overwriting.
